meta.title: Japanese — Kanji for JLPT N5
meta.subtitle: The 103 kanji of the first level — alongside the first words and N5
meta.desc: The kanji of the first level, one note each: 103 notes, each with TWO cards (kanji → meaning and readings; meaning and readings → kanji, to write from memory), each scheduled on its own. THE ORDER is the order the first words need them in: a kanji stands where the First Words deck and then JLPT N5 first write it, so studied a few cards a day beside those decks it arrives before, or with, its first word. 100 of the 103 are written on a front of those two decks; the other 3 (土、火、友) close the deck, commonest first. — WHICH KANJI, and the list is not official: the JLPT has published no kanji list since its 2010 revision. These are the kanji KANJIDIC2 marks with the former level 4, the first level of the pre-2010 test specification — the same measure that decides which words the N5 deck writes in kana. — The back gives the meanings, up to three on (Chinese-derived, in katakana) and three kun (native, in hiragana, the part written in kana in brackets) readings, the stroke count, the parts the kanji is drawn from, and up to four words from the first two decks that use it, with furigana, romaji, a meaning and a speaker. Stroke order is not shown. — Meanings, readings, stroke counts and levels: KANJIDIC2 (Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group, CC BY-SA 4.0). Parts: KanjiVG (Ulrich Apel, CC BY-SA 3.0). Words: Jonathan Waller's JLPT lists (CC BY) and JMdict (EDRDG, CC BY-SA 4.0), furigana JmdictFurigana (CC BY-SA 4.0).
